question: Two coordinators expanded capacity. Starting baseline: 34 items. Added 73 new units. Added 15 more from acquisition. Multiplied by 3 for replication. Multiplied by 4 for distribution. One distractor: competitor had 50 units. How many total units distributed?

A venue manager planned events. Starting bookings: 46 events. He subtracted 11 cancellations. He added 44 new bookings. He added 80 additional slots. He subtracted 139 conflicts. Morning through evening scheduling. A distractor: last month had 55 events. How many available events remain?

A book club began with 177 books. They sold 58 books at a garage sale. Then they purchased 66 new books. They gave away 171 books to a library. Seven books were damaged and discarded. Finally, they received a donation of 68 books. How many books does the club have now?

A single lemonade jar started the morning with 15 dollars in tip money. A busy morning left the jar with 7 times as much money. Then 39 more dollars were added from a bake sale table next to it. A matching donation multiplied the jar's total by 6. Finally, 25 more dollars came in from a raffle. A separate donation box nearby held about a dozen gift cards, unrelated to this jar's total. How much money was in that one jar in the end?

The stadium is divided into 109 blocks, every block has 7 rows, and every row holds 8 seats. At Saturday's match each seat holder was handed 5 raffle tickets on the way in. Half of all the tickets handed out were entered into the first draw of the evening. Each ticket in that first draw earned its holder 5 loyalty points. How many loyalty points were earned in the first draw?
A production started 225 units. Multiplied by 5. Added 4. Multiplied by 4. By 8. Lost 21052 error. What remain?

The candle workshop opened the morning with 6 crates on the bench, and every crate held 36 candles. By midday 130 candles had been sold to the gift shop in town. During the afternoon the chandler poured and finished 19 new candles, which joined the others on the bench. In the evening every candle was boxed with 2 long matches for the winter market. The packer added 16 spare matches to the box of supplies. How many matches were used or set aside in total?

The Beaumont Hotel counted 86 clean towels in the linen room first thing in the morning. Housekeeping brought up 40 towels from the laundry, then 12 more from the pool store, and later 21 from the staff room. During the afternoon guests took 56 towels from that room. In the evening the manager placed an order for the spa covering triple the towels still on the shelf, that is 3 times the number remaining. How many towels did the spa order cover?

A factory started with 134 units. They multiplied by 8 for daily production. They subtracted 355 units for returns. They added 39 units from quality improvements. They subtracted 297 units from a recalculation (measuring in adjusted production units). Throughout the day, morning production, afternoon quality control, and evening shipment preparation tracked adjusted units. Converting to measurement in time-ordered stages, what was the adjusted production count?

Rae had 221 glass beads and used 193 of them on a necklace. She gave 17 beads to her friend Sol, who then had more beads than Rae had left. Rae sold each of her remaining beads for 5 cents and received a 28-cent tip from the buyer. She checks her stall twice a day, and the same thing happened on each of 4 days. How many cents did Rae take over those 4 days?

A community theatre printed 183 programme booklets for the opening night of its new play. Every booklet contains 5 pages, and every page carries 6 photographs of the cast. Each photograph is built up from 6 separate layers of coloured ink. The printing machine lays down 5 ink layers on each pass of its roller. The theatre's hall seats 400 people. How many passes of the roller were needed to print the whole run of booklets?

A bakery began the morning with 4 ovens, each holding 164 rolls ready to bake, combining into one big batch. By midmorning, a shipping error caused 278 rolls to be sent to the wrong store, while a dozen spare baking trays sat unused in the back room. In the afternoon, 10 more rolls came out of a late batch, and later 13 more rolls were added from a walk-in order. Since the bakery weighs dough in ounces but sells rolls by count, the head baker kept two separate logs. By evening, 28 rolls were donated to a shelter. Overnight, 253 more rolls had to be discarded after a refrigeration failure. How many rolls were left the next morning?

At half past six in the morning, a newspaper depot sent out 9 carriers, each with 201 papers. By the afternoon, 234 papers had come back unsold and the rest had been sold. The depot earns 8 cents on every paper sold, and it counts its takings in cents even though a hundred cents make a dollar. In the evening the cashier changed all the day's cents into nickels, each nickel being worth 5 cents. How many nickels did the cashier end up with?

A city tracked the total number of parking permits issued downtown, starting with 156 permits already issued this year. A spring renewal wave added 45 more permits. A summer wave added 9 more. A batch of expired permits then removed 74 from the tracked total. A fall renewal wave added 74 more permits back. The permits were then split evenly among 6 parking zones, and only Zone 1's count was tracked from then on — the city noted this in its report as converting citywide permits into a per-zone count, a simple unit change. Finally, a zone expansion multiplied the tracked zone's count by 5. How many permits did Zone 1's tracked count show after the expansion?

A project had 62 tasks initially. They multiplied by 8 to show daily capacity. They divided by 4 to create work groups. Then multiplied by 5 for intensive tracking. Finally, they multiplied by 7 to show total work hours, then added 42 more. A competing project had 500 tasks but separate. How many work hours total including buffer?

A charity run had 206 registered runners. Then 68 more registered online, 25 signed up at the school, 61 joined through a company team, and 10 registered on the morning of the race. A dozen volunteers handed out water along the 21 kilometre route. The organizers divided all the runners equally into 5 starting waves. How many runners are in the first wave?

Nina sold 49 raffle tickets at 5 dollars each on the first day of the school fair. A local shop then added a 67 dollar donation to that day's takings. Each of the 4 days of the fair brought in exactly the same amount as the first day, so the fair's whole total came to 4 times that figure. The total was shared equally among 4 local charities. One of those charities is run by Carlos, who raised far less than Nina did at his own stall, and it later received a 56 dollar gift and then a 42 dollar gift. The fair also sold 310 hot dogs. How many dollars does Carlos's charity have from all of this?

On Saturday morning a scout group filled 131 hampers for the food bank, with 8 tins packed in every hamper. Before lunch a supermarket donated 14 loose tins. In the afternoon a church collection added 75 tins to the pile, and in the evening a delivery van brought 64 more. A dozen volunteers were sorting the shelves all day. How many tins does the food bank have?

A charity had raised $239 by the first hour, tallied over 60 minutes, or 1 hour, of the telethon, even though 500 people tuned in. A second hour added $77 more. A third hour added $68 more. A fourth hour added $69 more. The charity then spent $188 on printing costs. Finally, $67 more was spent on shipping fees. How much money did the charity have left?

A stock was 70 units. In the morning, 24 were sold. By midday, the remaining doubled. By afternoon, 56 were added. By late afternoon, 21 more arrived. By evening, 24 were added. How many (doubling as a unit)?

A theatre printed 221 programmes for each of the 2 opening nights, so the print run was double the single-night figure. Ushers handed out 313 programmes over those two nights. A stagehand then found 50 unopened programmes in a props box and added them to the pile. The theatre has 18 rows in the stalls, and the box office records running times in minutes rather than in hours. For the tour the printer produced triple the surviving pile, making 3 copies of every programme. Later 235 of those copies were sent for recycling. How many programmes remained?

Sam packed 68 apples for a group hiking trip. Along the trail, 52 more apples were added from a farm stand they passed. At base camp, three other hiking groups combined their apple supplies equally with Sam's, making the total four times as large. That evening, 38 more apples were donated by a passing trail crew. Finally, 40 more apples arrived with the last group to reach camp. How many apples were in the group's supply by the end?

A school ordered 5 boxes of exercise books with 61 books in each box. It sent 75 of the books over to the annexe. The stationery cupboard gave up 52 more books, a parent donated 35, and a bookshop added 18. The school has 9 classrooms. How many exercise books does the school have?

Diego was cataloguing rare trading cards for his shop, starting with 134 cards in a single binder. A booster restock left him with 5 times as many cards as before. He then sold 234 cards to a passing collector. A friend gave him 8 more cards found in an old drawer. That evening, a rival dealer named Wallace, who had exactly half as many cards as Diego started with, watched enviously as a warehouse delivery gave Diego 6 times as many cards as he then had. A nearby table displayed a sticker album for 17 dollars, which nobody bought. How many cards did Diego end up with?

A warehouse had 209 boxes of tiles delivered for a renovation project. A quality check removed 20 damaged boxes. A second delivery brought in 24 more boxes. A third delivery added 27 more boxes, arriving after a drive that took '180 minutes, or three hours.' The boxes were then split evenly into 3 job sites, and only one site's supply was tracked. A final bulk order turned every box at that site into 6 boxes. How many boxes of tiles were at that site after the final bulk order?
